conclusion: The pre-registered Gaussian training-noise intervention did not reduce the reference-to-Q.ANT prediction disagreement at fixed QFourier g4. Mean disagreement was 323.0 with no noise and 325.67 with both noise_std=0.02 and 0.04. Mean Q.ANT accuracy changed only marginally from 0.82987 to 0.83013 and 0.83043, respectively. These small accuracy changes do not establish a robustness benefit across three seeds.
interpretation: The primary robustness criterion failed: neither pre-registered noise level lowered mean disagreement relative to the no-noise baseline.
The highest tested noise level improved mean Q.ANT accuracy by only about 0.057 percentage points versus no noise, while mean disagreement increased by about 2.67 predictions per 10,000.
Effects vary by seed: noise sometimes reduces disagreement and sometimes increases it, providing no consistent cross-seed direction.
The exact-cosine reference accuracy is essentially unchanged, so the intervention did not materially alter ordinary reference performance.
The Exp011/Exp012 evidence points away from simple output-noise regularization as the solution to the exact-cosine versus Q.ANT-periodic mismatch.
next_direction: Investigate the mismatch directly rather than increasing grid size or merely injecting output noise. A clean next experiment should characterize where calc_kan_layer_fprop's periodic response differs from exact cosine over the activation/input ranges actually encountered by trained g4 models, then use that measured discrepancy to formulate a Q.ANT-aligned training surrogate before testing another learning intervention.
limitations: Q.ANT CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Three seeds and three epochs limit precision.
The tested noise is applied to the layer output during training; other robustness mechanisms remain untested.
